# cash

> A Python cache that re-runs only what changed. Two paths: `@cash.cache` caches
> a function call in scripts and modules, keyed on its arguments, its source and
> the source of the helpers it calls, and writes every result to disk.
> In a notebook, a first cell holding only `import cash` and `%cash_on` makes
> every statement below it cache itself, keyed on its code, its inputs and the
> files it reads.

## If you are a coding agent

Read this page first. `cash.help()` returns the same text in a running kernel:

- [Using cash — a guide for coding agents](docs/for-coding-agents.md)

For headless notebook runs (papermill, nbconvert), the first cell is exactly
`import cash`, `%cash_on` and `%cash_badge print`. The default badge is an HTML
widget that headless runs strip, and statements in the `%cash_on` cell are
never cached.

## Decorator

- [Quick start: decorator](docs/getting-started/quickstart-script.md): the first cached function.
- [`@cash.cache` guide](docs/decorator.md): parameters, what invalidates a result, where results are stored.
- [Warnings](docs/warnings.md): every warning code, such as `KEY-UNHASHABLE-ARG`.

## Notebook

- [Quick start: notebook](docs/getting-started/quickstart-notebook.md): turning on `%cash_on`.
- [Notebook guide](docs/notebook_caching_api.md#what-gets-cached): what a statement caches, refuses, or keys on.
- [Magic commands](docs/magics.md): `%cash_on`, `%cash_badge`, `%cash_stats` and the rest.
- [Annotations](docs/annotations.md): the `# @cash:` per-statement directives.
- [Reading the badge](docs/badges.md): statuses and "why did this re-run?".
- [Writing cache-safe cells](docs/known-limitations.md): patterns cash cannot see, and how to avoid them.
- [Cost model](docs/cost-model.md): which statements are cached, and the 0.1 s floor for writing them to disk.
